section.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains that the preface about light and name in the maamar hints that the superiority of "Echad" over "Yachid" is primarily when it also includes the aspect of "Yachid."
section.t: And it may be said,
that this—that in order to explain the superiority of Echad relative to Yachid, [the maamar] first introduces
(in the maamar)
the concept of light and name,
and that the main superiority of name is when it also contains the superiority of light—
is in order to hint
that this is also the case regarding the concept of Echad and Yachid,
that although the advantage of Echad over Yachid is also in the aspect of Echad as it is in itself,
nevertheless,
the main superiority in this is when it also contains the aspect of Yachid.
For the advantage in the aspect of Echad
(as it is in itself),
that even the worlds are nullified and unified,
does not have the quality of revelation.
Because this—that the nullification of Echad is not a nullification to the ultimate degree like the nullification of Yachid
(for in the nullification of Echad, the worlds appear as existent, and their nullification is like something additional to their existence)—
is due to the fact that the revelation of Ein Sof does not shine within them.
And the main superiority is that even in the worlds that came into being through the tzimtzum, the revelation of Ein Sof, which is above the tzimtzum, shines,
and the revelation is not in a manner that they are nullified from their existence, but rather that although they are in their existence, they are nullified to the ultimate degree
in the manner of the nullification of Yachid.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: To have the superiority of light within name (and the union of Echad and Yachid) requires drawing from Atzmus, which is above even name.
section.t: Now, in order that within name there should also be the superiority of light
[and likewise the union of Echad and Yachid],
this is through the drawing down of Atzmus, which is above even name.
For name, in itself, is concealment and cannot be in revelation,
and that which is drawn into revelation is through drawing into it from Atzmus.
And as explained by His Holy Honor, my father-in-law, the Rebbe
[in the maamar of Yud Tes Kislev,
which follows the maamar beginning "Atah Echad" of Tes Kislev],
that this—that Israel are called "those who sanctify Your name"—is because they draw into the name from the holiness of Atzmus,
the drawing of "Atah Kadosh" into "Shimcha Kadosh."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The conclusion of the prayer "Atah Echad" ("Yekadishu es Shimecha") relates to its beginning in two ways: through drawing from Atzmus, and as the actual result of that drawing.
section.t: Based on this, we may explain that the conclusion of the prayer "Atah Echad" is "Yekadishu es Shimecha,"
and the connection of the conclusion of the prayer to its beginning is in two matters.
For this—that Israel, a singular nation, draw down that "Atah Echad" and "Shimcha Echad"
(in a manner that within Echad there is also the revelation of Yachid, as in section 6 above)—
is through the drawing of the power of Atzmus—"Yekadishu es Shimecha."
And through Israel, a singular nation, drawing down "Atah Echad" and "Shimcha Echad,"
by this "Yekadishu es Shimecha" is actualized,
the drawing of "Atah Kadosh" into "Shimcha Kadosh."
And as explained in the maamar "Atah Echad" of the Baal HaHilula,
that the matter of "and upon their rest they will sanctify Your name" at the conclusion of the prayer "Atah Echad" is a level higher than all the matters preceding it.
